author: human
request:
Feature request: visits can currently only be created, never corrected. Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-5 is narrowed: cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope,
  but correcting its date and description is now in. Record the narrowing
  the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The edit form is reachable by its URL alone: the owner detail page gains
  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

Add editing for a booked visit:

- GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit shows the visit
  form prefilled with that visit's current date and description. Reuse the
  existing visit form template (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) and its `visit`
  model attribute.
- POST to the same URL validates like visit creation (description required,
  date in the future). On success it updates that visit in place — the pet
  must not gain an additional visit record — and redirects to the owner
  detail page. On validation failure it redisplays the form.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit's date and description can be corrected under the same rules as booking. The correction changes that visit in place, never adds another visit to the pet, and returns the reader to the owner's record.
acceptance_criteria: given a booked visit, when its correction form is opened, then the form shows that visit's current date and description
given a booked visit, when a description and a date later than today are submitted as its correction, then that visit carries them, the pet has no additional visit, and the owner's record is shown
given a blank description, when the correction is submitted, then the correction is refused, the form is shown again naming the description, and the visit is unchanged
given a date of today or earlier, when the correction is submitted, then the correction is refused, the form is shown again naming the date, and the visit is unchanged
Visits edge case 3: correcting a visit that does not exist, or that does not belong to the named pet and owner, is refused, and no visit is created or changed
non_goals: changing anything about a visit beyond its date and description, including moving it to another pet (NG-5)
any link or button to the correction form from the owner's record or any other page (owner decision, intake line 1: a visible entry point may come as a follow-up request)
a confirmation message after a successful correction (not stated by the owner; recorded as an open question)
any criterion on the pet's earlier-visits list while correcting (REQ-VIS-002 governs booking only)
notes: The owner-stated address, form template and model attribute for this slice are in the intake-decision at handoff.jsonl line 1. They are owner input for the design stage, not PRD content. Edge case 3 is the narrowest reading of the owner's 'updates that visit in place, the pet must not gain an additional visit record'. It matches booking edge case 1. Any wording shown on a correction must satisfy REQ-LANG-002. Open questions recorded in docs/prd.md: a visible entry point; whether a past-dated visit should be correctable, since the booking rules the owner chose require a future date; whether a correction is confirmed. New non-goal ADR docs/adr/2026-09-12-non-goal-visit-cancellation.md needs a row in the docs/adr/README.md index, which is outside this agent's write scope and falls to root or the system-design-expert. The 2026-08-08 non-goal ADR's Status line now points at the narrowing.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Visit correction applies an existing pattern with one adjustment. PetController's route-aware model-attribute factory (grep basis, IDE oracle not connected: PetController.java:75 findPet with @PathVariable(name = "petId", required = false)) moves into VisitController: the `visit` factory takes an optional visitId. Absent means booking, unchanged: a new visit is appended to the pet. Present means the pet's persisted visit, resolved through the pet within the owner the request names (system-design.md § Contracts, invariants paragraph). The write path is the existing sole one, owners.save(owner) cascading through Pet (§ Contracts, OwnerRepository row). The form template is reused unchanged, and correction adds no lifecycle state (§ State Machine). No new module, package, dependency, or ADR. Design-doc writes: REQ-VIS-003 joins the Pet, Visit, OwnerRepository, and VisitController Contracts rows; one invariant sentence; a derived Known Defects row for a pre-existing owner-rebinding gap, with a pointer from the Threat Model mass-assignment row; the ADR index row the product expert handed off.
integration_points: Entry points: GET and POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit on VisitController. Both render pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm with the `visit` model attribute. A successful POST returns redirect:/owners/{ownerId} and adds no flash message (prd-entry non-goal). The template form has no th:action, so it posts back to the correction address.

Binding target, correction POST: the pet's persisted Visit resolved by the factory, behind an @InitBinder("visit") allow-list of date and description. The controller-wide identifier disallow list stays (security-principles.md § Realization, mass-assignment row). The owner is taken from the model with binding disabled: @ModelAttribute(name = "owner", binding = false). It is never a binding target on this entry point.

Pet#getVisit(Integer): returns the pet's persisted visit with that identity, or null. Mirrors Owner#getPet(Integer), skipping new visits. The factory refuses a null result before anything is appended to the pet.

Refusal, edge case 3: an unknown visit, or a visit outside the named pet, raises IllegalArgumentException from the factory, the same form as the existing refusal of a pet outside the owner. With no controller advice in the @WebMvcTest slice, it propagates out of MockMvc perform(). Assert the throw, and assert that save is never invoked.

Repository boundary, OwnerRepository: keep the existing class-level @MockitoBean stub in VisitControllerTests as a conscious exception (testing-principles.md § Mocking Policy). A hand-written double would have to implement the whole inherited JpaRepository surface. A real repository would leave the @WebMvcTest slice that the prd-entry's test target names. Assert state on the fixture owner graph: after a correction, the pet has exactly one visit, carrying the submitted values. Assert 'unchanged' as save never invoked.

Framework transport: MockMvc, the one sanctioned harness (testing-principles.md § Mocking Policy). The fixture pet needs a persisted visit with its id set; edge case 3 needs a visit id outside that pet.

patterns.description: Route-aware model-attribute factory: an optional path variable chooses between a new object and the persisted one. Apply the same shape to the `visit` factory in VisitController.
Lookup by identity over the aggregate's children, skipping new ones and returning null when absent. Pet#getVisit(Integer) mirrors it.
The non-future date rejection with error code typeMismatch.visitDate. Booking and correction share this one check; extract it to a private method in the Refactor step, not a second copy.

risks.risk: The `visit` factory runs before every handler in VisitController and appends a new visit to the pet. Left unchanged on the correction route, the save would cascade an additional blank visit, breaking 'the pet has no additional visit'.
risks.mitigation: Make the factory route-aware (PetController.java:75 pattern). With a visitId present it resolves the existing visit and appends nothing. This keeps the Contracts invariant that Visit is persisted only through cascade from Owner (system-design.md § Contracts).

risks.risk: The booking handler's @ModelAttribute Owner parameter binds request fields onto the owner and then saves it. A copied handler signature would carry that gap into correction.
risks.mitigation: The correction POST reads the owner with binding disabled, and only the `visit` binder carries an allow-list (security-principles.md § Realization, mass-assignment row). The pre-existing gap is recorded under system-design.md § Known Defects and is not fixed in this slice.

risks.risk: A refused correction binds the rejected values onto the in-memory visit. The criterion says the visit is unchanged.
risks.mitigation: The graph is detached (system-design.md § Persistence: open-in-view is disabled). Nothing reaches the store without a save, so the error path returns before save. The refusal tests assert that save is never invoked; they do not assert the fixture's field values.

risks.risk: Trusting identifiers across requests: a correction POST acting on a visit that the GET validated.
risks.mitigation: Each request re-resolves the owner, the pet, and the visit through the factory (security-principles.md § Realization, cross-request state row).

risks.risk: The error page renders the exception message (system-design.md § Known Defects, REQ-SYS-002 row).
risks.mitigation: The refusal message carries identifiers only, like the existing owner and pet refusals (security-principles.md § Realization, secret-disclosure row).

notes: Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records exist in the log; skipped. Template: no change is needed to meet the criteria. The heading already drops 'New' for a persisted visit. The submit label stays #{addVisit}. A correction-specific label is wording the owner did not state, and a new key would have to reach all eleven bundles (REQ-LANG-002). Raise it with the entry-point follow-up; do not add it here. Also accepted without mitigation: on a refused correction, the Previous Visits list shows the rejected values for the visit being corrected, because it is the same instance; the prd-entry puts that list outside its criteria. Concurrent corrections are last-write-wins, since no entity carries a version column; owner and pet edits already behave this way. The new Known Defects row (owner rebinding through pet creation, pet edit, and visit booking) is derived from Spring's model-attribute binding semantics and not confirmed by a test. It is a candidate for a separate slice. ADR index: added the row for the 2026-09-12 non-goal ADR, and marked the 2026-08-08 row's status as NG-5 narrowed, matching that ADR's Status line.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Low, pre-existing, and now also reachable via correction: Visit.description has only @NotBlank with no @Size, while the h2 and mysql schemas cap it at VARCHAR(255) (db/h2/schema.sql:62 `description VARCHAR(255)`). An overlong correction is therefore refused by the database rather than by form validation. This was not exercised at runtime in this review; the likely effect is a failed update and an error page, with the visit unchanged. A length constraint would change the shared booking rule too, so it belongs to a future booking-validation slice, not this one.
approved_aspects: Mass assignment: the change makes the visit binder stricter. The pre-existing global deny-list stays in place (VisitController.java:55 `dataBinder.setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id");`), and the new `@InitBinder("visit")` allow-list (VisitController.java:62 `dataBinder.setAllowedFields("date", "description");`) narrows binding on both the booking route and the correction route. The template's hidden `petId` input is not bindable on either.

The owner is not bound on the new correction POST: VisitController.java:138 `@ModelAttribute(name = "owner", binding = false) Owner owner`. So the `owners.save(owner)` on that route only persists the loaded owner graph plus the bound visit. The known pre-existing owner rewrite through visit booking (system-design.md threat-model row 'Pet and visit booking submissions can rewrite the owner') is not extended to the new route. The booking route's `@ModelAttribute Owner owner` (VisitController.java:116) is unchanged baseline.

Ownership and cross-request trust: loadPetWithVisit re-resolves owner -> pet -> visit on every request. The owner comes from `owners.findById(ownerId)`, the pet from `owner.getPet(petId)`, and the visit from `pet.getVisit(visitId)`, which only matches persisted visits in that pet's own collection (Pet.java `if (!visit.isNew() && Objects.equals(visit.getId(), id))`). A visitId outside the named pet or owner throws before binding or save, which meets PRD edge case 3 and the security-principles 'Trusting cross-request state' row. The test `theVisitCorrectionShouldBeRefusedForAVisitOutsideTheNamedPet` (VisitControllerTests.java:176) covers it.

Validation parity: the correction route carries `@Valid Visit visit` and the same `rejectDateNotInTheFuture` check as booking, so @NotBlank and the future-date rule hold on every path that persists a visit. With `spring.jpa.open-in-view=false` (application.properties:11), a rejected correction mutates only a detached entity and nothing is saved.

Output escaping: createOrUpdateVisitForm.html renders every user-derived value through `th:text` (pet name, owner name, visit description). A grep for `utext` and `__${` across src/main/java and templates/pets found no match, so there is no unescaped output and no request text in preprocessing. The new exception message holds only int/Integer path ids, so nothing sensitive reaches the error page.

Injection and dangerous sinks: the change adds no query text, shell, file, or deserialization sink. A grep for `Runtime|ProcessBuilder|exec(` in src/main/java matched only the AOT `RuntimeHints` imports and CrashController's `RuntimeException`. No credentials or secrets were added in the diff.

Surface: one new GET/POST pair at /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit, as open as every other route by the documented demonstration baseline (system-design.md Threat Model 'Unauthenticated data modification' names the visit edit routes). Management exposure is unchanged.

Supply chain: build.gradle and pom.xml are unchanged in this diff (`git diff --stat` on them was empty), so no dependency was added. OWASP dependencyCheckAnalyze is not configured (no dependencyCheck task in `./gradlew tasks --all`), so no NVD match ran in this review. Resolved runtimeClasspath: spring-boot-starter-webmvc 4.1.1, spring-webmvc 7.0.9, jackson-databind 3.1.5, thymeleaf-spring6 3.1.5.RELEASE, hibernate-core 7.4.5.Final.

author: change-grader
summary: add in-place correction of a booked visit's date and description

blast_radius.note: The change is small (one module, two prod files, 85 prod lines, no sensitive-glob paths), but it lands on VisitController, the declared security surface. It adds an unauthenticated GET/POST write route on a persisted entity, and it rewrites loadPetWithVisit, the @ModelAttribute factory that runs before every handler in the controller, so the existing booking flow now goes through the new code too.

semantic_surprise.note: I read every prod hunk. The booking branch still appends a new Visit exactly as before, and the correction branch appends nothing. The lookup is scoped to the pet within the named owner and skips unsaved visits, and the date check was moved verbatim into rejectDateNotInTheFuture with its operator intact. The template has no th:action, so the correction posts back to its own URL. The owner is bound with binding=false, open-in-view is false (application.properties:11), so a refused correction's in-memory edits are never flushed, and Pet.visits is EAGER, so the lookup works on the detached graph. The visit allow-list also covers booking, but Visit has no bindable fields besides date and description, so booking does not actually change. The only visible surprises are cosmetic (the reused form still says Add Visit) and the documented rule that a past-dated visit can only be corrected by moving it to a future date.

test_adequacy.note: The tests check real outcomes. The in-place test compares the pet's whole visit set with containsExactly, so it would fail if a second visit were added. They cover the date boundary (today and yesterday), a blank description, a sibling pet's visit, an unknown visit id, and an attempt to overwrite the owner's last name, and PetTests unit-tests the lookup, including skipping unsaved visits. The one gap is that persistence runs through a mocked OwnerRepository, so nothing checks against a real database that the merge updates the existing row rather than inserting a new one. The booking tests already work this way.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four reviewers the plan dispatched approved in round 1 with no findings, and the citations I checked resolve (VisitController.java:55, :62, :116, :138; VisitControllerTests.java:136, :176; db/h2/schema.sql:62; application.properties:11). The security reviewer did attach one caveat: Visit.description has no @Size limit while the column is VARCHAR(255), so an overlong correction would be refused by the database rather than the form. The reviewer did not test this at runtime, and the security brief does not record it as a known gap.

scope_deviation.note: There were no build retries, consultations, or design revisions. The prod edits match the design-block's declared paths and patterns, and the doc edits (narrowed NG-5 with its own ADR, PRD bullets and open questions, contract rows, and a derived Known Defects row for the existing owner-rebinding gap) are the writes the design-block declared. Owner decisions (URL-only access, reused template) were honored.

rationale: Read VisitController's rewritten loadPetWithVisit factory and the new visit binder. They add an unauthenticated write route and change the pre-handler that booking also runs through. I found no defect there. Before merging, also accept that past visits can only be corrected by moving them to a future date, and weigh the unbounded-description recommendation.
